slides.headline: 1) CREATE A CLAUDE.MD FILE AND IT NEVER FORGETS YOUR RULES
slides.body:
Your Claude session wastes 10 minutes re-explaining context. He shows one file that kills it.

"Create a CLAUDE.md in my project root. Add my stack, naming rules, and what to never touch."

slides.headline: 2) MAKE CLAUDE WRITE A PLAN BEFORE IT TOUCHES YOUR CODE
slides.body:
He shows Claude rewriting 12 files when asked to fix one bug. One prompt stops this.

"Before writing any code, write a plan. List every file you'll change. Stop there."

slides.headline: 3) TELL CLAUDE EXACTLY WHICH FILES IT IS ALLOWED TO CHANGE
slides.body:
He shows Claude editing the payment module when only the login was broken. Your code is next.

"Only edit files inside /src/auth. Do not touch /src/payments or any file I haven't listed."

slides.headline: 4) ULTRATHINK
slides.body:
One word triggers a deeper reasoning mode. He adds it to every hard problem. It works

"Ultrathink: why is my auth middleware failing silently on token expiry?"

slides.headline: 5) BUILD ONE PIECE AT A TIME THEN WAIT FOR YOUR REVIEW
slides.body:
He builds features in chunks. Each piece gets reviewed before the next starts.

"Build only the database schema now. Stop when done. Wait for my review before the next step."

slides.headline: 6) PASTE THE WHOLE ERROR PLUS WHAT YOU ALREADY TRIED
slides.body:
Short questions get short answers. He pastes the full error and what failed. One shot, every time.

"Here is the error: [paste]. Here is the file: [paste]. I already tried [X]. Fix it"

caption:
Swipe through all 6. The engineer who built Claude Code released a video that beats $300 courses. Everything is free. 🔖

This post covers creating a CLAUDE.md memory file your project reads every session, writing a plan before any code starts, locking exactly which files Claude can and cannot touch, the ultrathink command for harder reasoning problems, building one piece at a time with review stops, and giving Claude the full error plus what you already tried.

Most people use Claude Code like a search engine and get thin answers. The engineer who built it shows that knowing these six rules is worth more than any $300 course. Running a business? DM us "AI" and we'll show you what this could do for yours.
